newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-SPANISH LEAGUE FIXTURES AT THE WEEKEND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SPANISH LEAGUE FIXTURES AT THE WEEKEND.

text.p: Matches scheduled for this weekend in the Spanish first division: (kick-off times gmt, league positions in parentheses)
playing Saturday:
Deportivo Coruna (4) v Sevilla (21) kickoff 1830 gmt
Deportivo have won their last five consecutive home games, but will have to be on their guard against a Sevilla side that is showing signs of revival.
playing Sunday:
Real Madrid (1) v Sporting Gijon (19) 1600

League leaders Real are still in a state of shock from the announcement that coach Fabio Capello will leave the club at the end of the season, and Real supporters look set to give the Italian coach an angry reception.
Espanyol (16) v Real Sociedad (8) 1600

Real Sociedad have taken a draw from their last two visits to the Sarria stadium, but are in a free-fall that contrasts with the run of good form of an Espanyol side that will be without Romanian striker Florin Raducioiu.
Athletic Bilbao (7) v Valladolid (6) 1700
Athletic have turned around a habit that saw them drawing nearly half their games, and will be looking for a result against UEFA Cup rivals Valladolid.
Hercules (20) v Logrones (22) 1700

Two teams that seem doomed to fall straight back down to the second division meet in a game that is all the more important because results of games between teams count ahead of goal difference in determining final standings.
Real Betis (3) v Compostela (13) 1700
Betis have never lost at home to Compostela, but have made a habit of coming unstuck against weaker opposition in the Benito Villamarin stadium.
Rayo Vallecano (17) v Tenerife (9) 1700

Tenerife must refocus on the league and next season's UEFA Cup after crashing out of this year's competition to Schalke 04, while Rayo Vallecano are still fighting to avoid being one of four teams automatically relegated.
Oviedo (18) v Zaragoza (14) 1700
Oviedo have slipped inexplicably into the danger area, and will definitely be without midfielders Jose Gay and Berto Martinez, while defender Fernando Gamboa is also doubtful.
Racing Santander (11) v Atletico Madrid (5) 1700
Racing will have to look for replacements for injured defenders Gabriel Schurrer and Diego Lopez, against an Atletico team that still has some work to do to guarantee a UEFA Cup place.
Celta Vigo (12) v Valencia (10) 1730
Valencia have been rocked this week by mutual recriminations between coach Jorge Valdano and club owner Paco Roig, and desperately need a win to keep their UEFA Cup aspirations alive.
playing Monday:
Extremadura (15) v Barcelona (2) 1930

Extremadura, who just three months ago were near-certain relegation candidates, will look to stretch their nine-game unbeaten streak at home against a Barcelona side that will be looking to capitalise on instability at leaders Real Madrid.
